answer.how: The cycle was already there in the first commit, b3ae88d60f ('publish source-free OrionTV'), which imported the whole desktop app in one go. In that commit MainWindow (namespace OrionTV.Desktop.App) does `using OrionTV.Desktop.App.Views` and creates HomeView, LiveView, SettingsView, PlayerView and the other pages in CreateView. That is the App → Views edge. The Views depend back on the root namespace: AiImportDialog calls AiCliLauncher.ResolveDocsDirectory/Launch/LaunchDiscovery, and LiveView and PlayerView use PlaybackController and the PlaybackState enum declared in PlaybackController.cs. Later commits made both directions stronger. f1bbae77f7 grew MainWindow by about 200 lines and rewrote PlayerView (+1070 lines), which now handles PlaybackState in Controller_StateChanged. e137971afc added SectionNavigationState in MainWindow and the INavigationVisibilityAware interface in Navigation.cs, which LiveView now implements.

timeline.change: Initial import: MainWindow creates all Views (App→Views); AiImportDialog calls AiCliLauncher, and LiveView/PlayerView use PlaybackController/PlaybackState (Views→App)
MainWindow and PlayerView greatly expanded; PlayerView adds more state handling against App's PlaybackState/PlaybackController
MainWindow adds per-section view state over the Views; LiveView implements the new App-level INavigationVisibilityAware interface

answer.why_problematic: The shell (MainWindow) builds the pages, and the pages reach back into root-namespace services (AiCliLauncher) and playback types (PlaybackState), so neither namespace can be built or tested without the other. A change to PlaybackController's state model or to MainWindow's navigation ripples into LiveView and PlayerView and back again. As a result, no page can be reused outside this one window.

answer.how: This cycle was also present from the initial import, b3ae88d60f. It runs App → Views (MainWindow creates PlayerView and the other pages), then Views → LocalPlayback (PlayerView does `using OrionTV.Desktop.App.LocalPlayback`, hosts MpvHost in XAML and creates `new MpvLocalEngine(hwnd, Dispatcher)`), then LocalPlayback → App (MpvLocalEngine keeps `PlaybackState _state = PlaybackState.Idle`, and PlaybackState is the enum declared in App/PlaybackController.cs). The Views → App edges of smell 1 (AiImportDialog→AiCliLauncher, LiveView/PlayerView→PlaybackState) also take part. Later commits kept the cycle alive and made it larger: e1991e7308 (+293 lines), f1bbae77f7 and 96434d1c40 reworked MpvLocalEngine and its state machine, which is still written in terms of App's PlaybackState. Several of the same commits (e1991e7308, f1bbae77f7, 96434d1c40) also extended PlayerView's use of the mpv engine.

MpvLocalEngine (+293 lines) and PlayerView extended; the engine keeps reporting state through App's PlaybackState
MpvLocalEngine, PlayerView, PlaybackController and MainWindow all extended further
MpvLocalEngine extended again (+176 lines) and still coupled to App's PlaybackState

answer.why_problematic: The mpv playback engine is meant to be a low-level, reusable component. Here it depends on an enum that lives next to the LibVLC PlaybackController in the app shell, and the shell reaches it only through PlayerView. Because of this three-namespace loop, the local playback engine cannot be extracted or tested without the views and the main window. Any change to PlaybackState also affects both playback back-ends and the player UI.

answer.why_problematic: OrionTV.Desktop.Core is a single catch-all assembly that holds HTTP clients for several VOD protocols, Douban metadata, live-stream health probing, HLS ad skipping, protocols for three different AI translation and speech-to-text vendors, playback startup and resume policies, and JSON file persistence. These concerns have nothing to do with each other. Any change, such as a Gemini protocol tweak or a new MacCMS field, touches and rebuilds the same component that the WPF app depends on everywhere. The component cannot be reused in parts (for example, only the source clients), and with 56 types and no sub-namespaces it is hard to see where a responsibility lives.

answer.why_problematic: The single OrionTV.Desktop.Tests project has become the place where every release commit (1.3.15, 1.3.16, 1.3.17) puts its tests, so it grows with each feature and has no internal structure: all 22 files sit flat in one namespace. Large files such as VodCacheServiceTests (over 880 lines with three nested helpers) and ChannelHealthScoringTests (seven nested handlers) make it hard to find, maintain and selectively run the tests for one subsystem. The test project also depends on both App and Core, so most changes anywhere in the product touch it.
